title: Floods and avalanches devastate the Nepal-Tibet border
subtitle: Glacier collapse in the Himalayas causes mass destruction, thousands missing, and strains diplomatic relations in the region.
excerpt: Disasters caused by a glacial collapse in the Himalayas leave thousands dead and missing on the border between Nepal and Tibet.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: G1, Gazeta do Povo, Folha de S.Paulo
contentHtml:
A series of flash floods and landslides triggered by the collapse of a glacier in the Himalayas has devastated the border between China and Nepal, sparking a major humanitarian crisis. The physical disaster was accompanied by a strict digital blackout in Tibet, while rescue teams continue their search for thousands of missing people.

The devastating impact of the tragedy in the region

The death toll from the floods and landslides that struck the Himalayan region has surpassed the one thousand mark, according to updated provisional figures. Rescue teams continue to search for survivors amid the mud and debris, while the Nepalese government has begun mass burials for some of the unidentified victims due to overcrowded morgues.

Search efforts in Nepal are also focusing on tunnels where hundreds of workers employed in the area could be trapped. On the Nepalese side, floods and avalanches destroyed entire communities, bridges, villages, and dozens of schools, jeopardizing the education of thousands of students.

The quick action of a school principal

In the Nuwakot district of northern Nepal, principal Rajendra Dawadi managed to save at least 900 students by ordering an emergency evacuation at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School. The educator received warnings that a massive torrent of water was surging down the Trishuli River valley and decided to halt classes immediately.

Dawadi rang the bell and directed students and staff to head toward higher ground on a nearby hill. The water began rising rapidly as the group fled, and the school building was ultimately completely swept away by the torrent of mud, rocks, and debris shortly after the evacuation.

Digital censorship and narrative control in Tibet

On the other side of the border, in the Tibet Autonomous Region, the physical disaster was quickly accompanied by a digital blackout. The Chinese government's information control apparatus used advanced image recognition technology and artificial intelligence to block raw videos and survivor accounts.

Chinese platforms removed posts about the destruction and hid images related to the National Gate and Gyirong Port. The algorithm flooded networks with content from state media and official reports, such as coordinated meetings by the country's leadership, turning the tragedy into a showcase of state response.

Structural failures and diplomatic friction

The suppression of information sought to conceal structural vulnerabilities and a history of negligence in the region, which had already recorded landslides and floods in previous years at the same commercial port. The lack of cross-border data sharing generated strong friction with Nepal.

A Nepalese journalist publicly criticized Beijing for failing to provide early warnings that could have prevented massive loss of life in the neighboring country. The Chinese embassy in Nepal rejected the accusations, calling the claims groundless, while families continue to search for thousands of missing loved ones.

With information from G1, Gazeta do Povo, Folha de S.Paulo.
